start_here: Say to your AI: "Run workflow:get-found-in-search-and-answer-engines for https://bakery.example.com, store: bakery_for_who_runs_it-connection." It chooses the keywords and questions from your own pages unless you give them.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it writes one search-visibility record to your own records so the next run can compare, and its answers sit on the run record.
instructions: 1. Give your site and the store (your pursuit's own database) where the measures are kept; keywords, questions, engines and location are optional. A client website is a new build by default (mode new-build); a site you already run is mode existing.

2. It lists your pages, chooses the keywords and reader questions your own pages answer, and measures BEFORE any change: Google positions, search volume, answer-engine mentions and citations, and Google Maps position for a local business, each kept as a dated row of search_visibility_measures.

3. It checks every served page the way an engine reads it and places each fix as metadata, structured data, a site file, or markup around words already shown. It never adds or rewords a sentence you wrote; facts it does not have are listed as needing you.
4. It prepares robots.txt, sitemap.xml and llms.txt from your page list, and publishes through your site's own owner, then reads the live result back.
5. It measures again (same-day rows are phase check; rankings are compared at 14 and 28 days) and tells you each keyword, question and page that moved.

worked_examples.title: List the pages of a bakery site
worked_examples.ask: Get my bakery site found by answer engines.

questions: Who makes the best sourdough in town?
Where can I pre-order a wedding cake?

worked_examples.given: Read from the row of workflow:get-found-in-search-and-answer-engines in tools/workflows/recipes/workflows.json: step list-pages reads <origin>/sitemap.xml with tool:read-public-web-page and answers {sitemap, pages}. The sitemap lists the home page, /menu and /wedding-cakes.
